gaps.sentence: I wish you ___ so pessimistic about the project.
gaps.hint: a wish about a present attitude
gaps.explanation: Wishes about present states use 'were': were not.

gaps.sentence: As long as nobody ___, we will finish before lunch.
gaps.hint: as long as plus a present verb
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' clauses take the present simple: objects.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more at university!
gaps.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' — regret about a past failure.

gaps.sentence: She'd be a great lawyer if she ___ more patient.
gaps.explanation: Second conditional with 'be': 'were' for all persons.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me tonight, I will send you the files first thing.
gaps.explanation: A realistic future condition uses the present simple after 'if': email.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ a red light, you must stop.
gaps.explanation: General rules use the present simple in the if-clause: come to.

gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.
